acv.quote: Two hundred and fifty K ACV.

data.reason: Halima, the COO, picked the rival because it showed named people on call for on-sales. Our tiered support plans felt like 'a queue with a faster timer.' Jordan blames nothing but believes our platform was better.

trigger.action: Aim our message at the moment payments fail mid on-sale.
trigger.why: Payments failed four minutes into a Friday on-sale, and the old provider only replied after it ended.
trigger.quote: They got a reply after the on-sale was over.

decider.action: Show the COO who picks up, not just how the tech performs.
decider.why: Halima made the call alone in one meeting, and Ben, who wanted us, lost.
decider.quote: it was Halima's call and she made it in one meeting.

competitor.action: Bring the real account team, by name, into the early meetings.
competitor.why: Ben said the rival brought its own engineer and account lead. Jordan's 'over-promised' doubt is only his guess.
competitor.quote: A named solutions engineer and an account lead, in the room.

message.action: Replace the support tiers pitch with named people for on-sales.
message.why: Halima asked 'who's my person' and Jordan walked her through tiers and response times.
message.quote: so it's a queue with a faster timer.

proof.action: Build a written plan for what we do on on-sale morning.
proof.why: Halima asked to see it on paper, and Jordan had nothing, though he could have built one.
proof.quote: She wanted to see, on paper, what we do on an on-sale morning.

words.action: Say 'a name, not a queue' instead of 'support plans'.
words.why: Halima talked about who picks up when things break, and nobody said 'support'.
words.quote: I don't buy uptime, I buy what happens when it's down.
